overview: Booster Innovation Fund (BIF) is a managed investment scheme listed on the NZX Main Board since 2 March 2022, managed by Booster Investment Management Limited (BIML), a subsidiary of the ~$8bn-AUM Booster Group. It is effectively New Zealand's only listed, retail-accessible venture capital vehicle, investing in a portfolio of 40 (as at 31 March 2026) early-stage, unlisted companies built on IP originated or developed in New Zealand, spanning life sciences, materials, energy/clean-tech and information services technology. Net assets have grown from $7.62m at inception (FY2022) to $24.68m at FY2026, funded almost entirely by new unit subscriptions rather than by cash returned from realised investments.

business_model.summary: BIF is not an operating company but a closed-style venture capital fund. It earns unitholders a return purely through NAV appreciation (unrealised fair-value revaluations of its unlisted holdings, assessed by the Manager) since the portfolio has produced essentially no cash distributions to the Fund. New capital comes from unit applications (heavily from Booster's own KiwiSaver and Super schemes) and is deployed into new or follow-on early-stage rounds, mostly at 0-5% shareholdings, often via NZ Innovation Booster Limited Partnership (NZIB), a related-party co-investment vehicle with three university tech-transfer offices (Auckland UniServices joined December 2025, alongside Wellington UniVentures and Otago Innovation Limited).

revenue_streams.name: Unrealised fair-value gains on unlisted investments

business_model.customer_type: Retail and institutional NZ unitholders (PIE managed fund structure); underlying "customers" are the ~40 early-stage NZ companies the Fund invests in
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand-originated IP; several portfolio companies (e.g., BioLumic, Allegro Energy, Ferronova) are incorporated offshore (US/Australia) to access larger capital markets while IP/origin remains NZ

main_competitors: NZ Growth Capital Partners / Elevate NZ Venture Fund (fund-of-funds, Crown-backed, not directly retail-accessible)
Icehouse Ventures (Seed Fund IV, IVX growth fund - wholesale/institutional access)
Bridgewest Ventures (NZ$60m+ deep-tech venture fund, targeting offshore capital)
Direct wholesale/angel investment via AngelHQ, Global from Day One (GD1), Punakaiki Fund
Punakaiki Fund (another listed-adjacent NZ venture vehicle)
Australian/global specialist VCs co-investing in the same NZ deep-tech rounds
competitive_position.market_position: Effectively the only NZX-listed, retail-accessible pure-play venture capital fund in New Zealand; niche positioning rather than scale leadership in a small domestic VC market

moat_factors.description: PDS-based retail managed investment scheme structure with a listed unit is difficult and costly for a new entrant to replicate; BIF has first-mover status as NZX's only listed VC vehicle

moat_factors.factor: Deal-flow access via Booster Group and NZIB
moat_factors.description: Relationship with Auckland UniServices, Wellington UniVentures and Otago Innovation Limited via NZIB gives privileged access to university-spun-out deep tech, which retail investors cannot otherwise reach
Booster's own KiwiSaver Scheme (55.7% of units) and SuperScheme (8.9%) are the largest unitholders, meaning Booster's own default retirement savings are invested alongside retail unitholders
Booster's retail distribution network (200,000+ customers) can market BIF, but this is a distribution advantage for gathering assets, not a moat for the underlying venture returns

weaknesses: No genuine market-based price discovery: 100% of NAV is Level 3 manager-marked, unlisted holdings
Tiny scale ($24.7m net assets) limits ability to write meaningful cheques or maintain pro-rata ownership through future funding rounds
Almost total dependence on Booster's own related-party funds for both governance oversight and marginal buying demand for units
Illiquid secondary market — NZX trading is nominal; real liquidity is via Manager application/redemption at the struck unit price
Zero realised exits in over five years despite reporting cumulative unrealised gains

growth_drivers: Portfolio maturation: 60% of holdings by value are now in "Expansion" stage (up from a more seed/early-stage mix historically), which is when meaningful revaluations or exits typically begin to occur
Addition of Auckland UniServices to NZIB (Dec-2025) broadens deal pipeline across all three major NZ university tech-transfer offices
Minimum initial investment cut from $1,000 to $500 (Dec-2025 PDS) widens the retail funnel
Standalone Fund Investment Committee (from 5 June 2025, no longer a Booster group subcommittee) intended to improve governance and decision independence

Buoyant broader NZ venture funding backdrop: Icehouse Ventures closed a record NZ$70m Seed Fund IV and a NZ$122m IVX growth fund in 2025, Bridgewest raised NZ$60.2m for deep tech, and the Crown added a further $100m to the Elevate NZ Venture Fund in Budget 2025 — more follow-on capital increases the odds BIF's portfolio companies can raise up-rounds

Multiple portfolio companies showing commercial traction: Alimetry raised a US$18m Series A2 in late 2024 with FDA clearances and a CPT III reimbursement code; BioLumic expanding into South America; Calocurb's new US partnership targeted to double revenue; Tectrax/ZeroJet (merged as Wave Propulsion) expanding into Europe
Potential for a power-law outcome: a single large exit (e.g., Alimetry, Allegro Energy or Bontia Bio, the fund's largest disclosed stake at 10-15%) could materially re-rate the whole $24.7m NAV

business.description: Across FY2022-FY2026 the Fund has received just $568k of distributions (all in FY2022) against roughly $20m of net assets deployed; the venture exit thesis underpinning the NAV is entirely untested in cash terms

Most holdings are 0-5% stakes; the Fund often cannot fund its pro-rata share of future rounds in a capital-constrained NZ deep-tech ecosystem, risking dilution or write-off. FY2026's portfolio table already excludes an unstated number of companies now in liquidation or valued near nil

business.risk: Concentration in a small domestic ecosystem
business.description: 100% NZ-originated IP means correlated exposure to a small pool of local research institutions, deal-flow sources (NZIB, GD1, Icehouse) and follow-on investors

Companies placed into liquidation or valued at nil are dropped from the Scheme Property table entirely, so the published 40-holding portfolio overstates historical hit-rate versus the full universe of companies ever funded

financial.description: There is no listed market price for any underlying holding; NAV is entirely dependent on Manager judgement, informed by financing rounds, sales growth and business-plan progress rather than observable market transactions

Cash was just $326k (~1.3% of net assets) at FY2026 year-end; the Fund relies on fresh unit issuance to fund new acquisitions ($3.074m raised vs $2.585m deployed in FY2026) rather than internally generated cash
Some holdings (BioLumic Inc, Allegro Energy Pty, Ferronova Pty, Nutrition From Water Inc) are denominated in USD/AUD; FX translation moved net assets by -$4k in FY2026 and +$119k in FY2025

regulatory.description: MIS managers were removed from the mandatory climate reporting regime from 22 October 2025 (FY2025 was the last climate statement) — a compliance-cost relief rather than a risk, but signals an evolving regulatory perimeter

Extensive related-party dealings (Booster KiwiSaver/Super funding new units, NZIB co-investment structure, BFSL capital commitments) require ongoing arm's-length and disclosure compliance; any regulatory or FMA concern about related-party governance would be a reputational risk for a retail-facing scheme

macro.risk: Venture funding cycle / follow-on capital availability
macro.description: Portfolio companies depend on external capital markets (VC funds, corporates, Elevate-backed managers) for follow-on rounds; a downturn in global or NZ risk-capital appetite would directly impair BIF's ability to mark up or exit holdings

macro.risk: Interest rate sensitivity of early-stage valuations
macro.description: Higher-for-longer global rates compress venture valuation multiples broadly, which flows through to BIML's fair-value marks even though holdings are unlisted

Reported market prices show negligible trading range ($1.504-$1.508 over 52 weeks per Yahoo Finance), meaning unitholders needing liquidity outside the Manager's own application/redemption window may find no real market

execution.description: Multiple leadership changes in FY2026: Allan Yeo (Booster Group Managing Director) stepped off the BIML board 1 Dec 2025 and off Booster Financial Services 4 May 2026 (no longer a Senior Manager); Nic Craven stepped down as CIO (Apr-2025), replaced by Simon O'Grady (Sep-2025); Diana Papadopoulos became CEO in 2025. New group holding entities (Booster Group Limited, Booster Financial Services Group Limited) were inserted above BFSL on 31 Dec 2025

The Fund's Investment Committee became a standalone committee (5 June 2025) rather than a subcommittee of the wider Booster Investment Committee — an improvement in independence, but a change in decision process during the review period

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ venture capital funding is currently expansionary: Icehouse Ventures closed a record NZ$70m Seed Fund IV plus a NZ$122m IVX growth fund in 2025, Bridgewest Ventures raised ~NZ$60.2m (targeting NZ$100m) for a dedicated ANZ deep-tech fund in 2026, and the government topped up the Elevate NZ Venture Fund-of-funds with a further $100m in Budget 2025 (total committed ~$246m+ across 11 underlying funds since 2020, backing ~150 companies, ~41% deep tech). Deep-tech exit rates in ANZ (~6.5% via M&A/IPO) modestly exceed the broader tech average (~5.0%), but absolute exit volumes remain small and BIF itself has recorded no realised exits since listing.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — early-stage venture valuations and follow-on funding availability are highly sensitive to the broader risk-capital cycle; BIF's FY2025 NAV per unit fell 8.3% on revaluations alone, demonstrating that reported NAV is not a smooth or defensive metric
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high indirect sensitivity — higher discount rates and reduced VC risk appetite globally compress private valuation multiples, which flow through to BIML's marks even without a listed reference price
key_input_costs: Follow-on venture capital availability (domestic and offshore)
USD/AUD exchange rates on offshore-incorporated holdings
Cost/availability of specialist deep-tech technical and regulatory expertise (e.g., FDA clearance costs for medtech holdings like Alimetry)

recent_developments.event: Manager issued 255,337 new units at $1.4759/unit, below the 31-March-2026 NAV of $1.5114 and below the 24-March-2026 adjusted NAV of ~$1.534, indicating a subsequent downward valuation move into Q1 FY2027

NZX announcement: Allan Yeo (Booster Group Managing Director) stepped off the Booster Financial Services Limited board effective 4 May 2026 and ceased to be a BIML Senior Manager, though he remains a director of ultimate parent Booster Group Limited; updated Senior Manager/Director list disclosed
Booster increased Fund NAV by ~$629,000 (2.6%, net of performance fee/tax allowance) ahead of the 26 March 2026 unit issue, lifting NAV per unit to approximately $1.534 from $1.496

Updated Product Disclosure Statement issued: minimum initial investment cut from $1,000 to $500; Auckland UniServices joined NZIB as a new investment partner, broadening the university deal pipeline; NZIB-held interests brought under the same valuation approval process as direct holdings
Allan Yeo stepped down from the BIML Board; Diana Papadopoulos appointed director (from alternate-director role), continuing as CEO

Booster group restructuring: Booster Group Limited and Booster Financial Services Group Limited inserted as new holding entities above Booster Financial Services Limited, which remains BIML's immediate parent
Government removed managed investment scheme managers from mandatory climate-reporting regime; FY2025 was BIF's final climate statement
Simon O'Grady appointed Chief Investment Officer of BIML, following Nic Craven's departure from the role in April 2025
Fund's Investment Committee became a standalone committee (previously a Booster Investment Committee subcommittee), with Dana McKenzie appointed a full member
Dispute resolution scheme provider changed from Financial Dispute Resolution Services to Financial Services Complaints Limited (FSCL)

Net assets rose to $24.68m (from $20.36m) on $1.756m unrealised fair-value gains, $3.074m of new unit proceeds and $2.585m of acquisitions; NAV per unit recovered to $1.5114 after FY2025's 8.3% decline; performance fee was $0 for the second consecutive year

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Report (year ended 31 March 2026) and 7 May 2026 NZX announcement

items.target: Payable only when NAV outperforms — $0 charged in both FY2025 and FY2026
items.notes: Fee structure is contractual (per Trust Deed/PDS), not formal earnings guidance; the fee has not triggered for two straight years, evidencing weak realised performance

items.target: Deliver a total return (net of fees, before tax) that outperforms the NZX 50 Index over rolling 15-year periods
items.notes: This is the Fund's stated long-run objective per its PDS/website; no shorter-term quantitative NAV or return target is disclosed by the Manager

items.target: No point estimate provided; Manager publishes ad hoc NZX valuation-adjustment updates when material re-marks occur (e.g., +2.6%/$629k in March 2026)
items.notes: Most recent disclosed unit issue price (July 2026) of $1.4759 is below the 31-March-2026 statutory NAV of $1.5114, implying a subsequent mark-down not yet reflected in annual report figures

guidance.management_commentary: No formal quantitative FY2027 revenue/earnings guidance is issued (the Fund does not report revenue/earnings in the operating-company sense). Management commentary in the FY2026 Annual Report emphasises pipeline broadening via Auckland UniServices joining NZIB, continuation of the standalone Investment Committee, and no material change to valuation/pricing methodology other than aligning NZIB-held interest approvals with direct holdings. The 7 May 2026 NZX release is purely a governance/personnel disclosure (Allan Yeo's reduced role) with no financial guidance content.

bull_case: Genuine diversification across 40 active early-stage NZ companies spanning life sciences, materials, energy and information services — a level of shots-on-goal a retail investor cannot otherwise assemble

Venture power-law dynamics mean a single scaled exit (e.g., Alimetry, which has FDA clearances, a CPT III reimbursement code and a 2024 US$18m raise, or Bontia Bio at the fund's largest 10-15% stake) could disproportionately re-rate the entire ~$24.7m NAV

Privileged, hard-to-replicate deal access via NZIB's partnerships with Auckland UniServices, Wellington UniVentures and Otago Innovation Limited gives exposure to university-originated deep tech unavailable to most retail or even wholesale investors
Minimum investment cut to $500 (Dec-2025) and no fund-level debt reduce the barrier to entry and remove leverage/refinancing risk

Strong sponsor alignment: Booster's own KiwiSaver Scheme (55.7%) and SuperScheme (8.9%) are the largest unitholders, meaning the manager's own default retirement-savings money is invested alongside retail unitholders, and a standalone Investment Committee (from June 2025) improves governance independence

Favourable macro backdrop for NZ venture capital: record Icehouse Ventures fund closes, a new Bridgewest deep-tech fund, and an extra $100m Crown commitment to the Elevate NZ Venture Fund in Budget 2025 all increase the pool of follow-on capital available to BIF's portfolio companies
bear_case: Zero cash has been realised from the portfolio in over five years bar a single $568k distribution in FY2022 — the entire reported NAV gain is unrealised and manager-marked, with the venture exit thesis completely unproven in cash terms

100% Level 3 valuation with no external market price test; the Manager's performance fee (waived the last two years but $201k in FY2023) is directly tied to the NAV it marks, an inherent conflict of interest

Market price already trades essentially at NAV ($1.508 vs $1.5114 FY2026 NAV), so there is no discount-to-NAV arbitrage available — the entire investment case rests on trusting the manager's NAV and its future compounding, not on buying assets cheaply

Survivorship bias: companies placed into liquidation or written to near-nil are dropped from the disclosed portfolio table entirely, likely flattering the visible track record versus the full universe of capital deployed

Related-party concentration: over 60% of units are held by Booster's own KiwiSaver/Super schemes, which are also effectively the marginal buyers funding new acquisitions via fresh unit subscriptions — this blurs whether unit demand reflects independent investor conviction or captive internal allocation

FY2025 showed NAV per unit can fall materially (-8.3%) in a single year purely from revaluation, and the July 2026 unit issue price ($1.4759) already sits below the audited 31-March-2026 NAV ($1.5114), suggesting further softening; the listing itself is effectively illiquid (52-week trading range of ~$1.504-$1.508), so unitholders needing an exit are reliant on the Manager's own redemption facility rather than a functioning secondary market
